historical_claims_to_preserve: Use the 2026-05-07 capture date from old raw line 2 even though the filename says 2025. Keep its raw citation and date the fully documented variant behavior. Checkout and Elements with Checkout Sessions retain the documented MX/MXN one-time Checkout constraints (old raw 18–50, 233–275), the valid email and Account/Customer parameter distinction in Checkout Elements (475–527), and the Session/client-secret identity distinct from the separately server-created MXN PaymentIntent and its client secret in Payment Intents Elements (958–1088).

Preserve the Checkout voucher redirect and Checkout Session events with the related PaymentIntent outcome (old raw 172–194). Mobile and Direct API use PaymentIntent confirmation to create or show the voucher, with the customer paying cash separately and success determined asynchronously. The iOS `.succeeded` and Android `PaymentResult.Completed` client callbacks in those examples signify voucher display (old raw 1429–1462, 1668–1720). React Native displays a voucher webview and treats `RequiresAction` as voucher creation while awaiting payment (old raw 1922–2004). Mobile and Direct API say a voucher cannot be cancelled before expiry (old raw 1474–1487, 1529–1533, 2294–2307, 2509–2513).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-oxxo-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-oxxo-accept-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-oxxo-accept-payment.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo/accept-a-payment`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo/accept-a-payment identifies OXXO as a Mexican payment method and routes Checkout, Elements with the Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents API, Direct API, and iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-21). The base index establishes those routes only. The 2026-05-07 capture documents in-store cash payment with a generated voucher, and for Checkout an MX business, MXN, payment mode and one-time line items (old raw lines 12-50). Checkout Session submission generates a voucher and later async success is the fulfillment signal (old raw lines 172-194). Elements with Checkout Sessions hands a server-created Session client secret to the client and requires a valid customer email to complete the Session (old raw lines 475-487), while Payment Intents Elements uses the server-created PaymentIntent and its client secret (old raw lines 271-305 and old raw lines 958-1088). The May Legacy Direct API requires the customer's full name and email, with each of the first and last names at least two characters (old raw lines 2195-2202). Direct API and mobile confirmation can issue or display the voucher while payment awaits the customer, and the server observes the later PaymentIntent outcome (old raw lines 1950-2029 and old raw lines 2195-2307). source-stripe-oxxo-accept-payment.md retains historical Checkout and expiry details but misses React Native and misstates Direct API billing details, Legacy status and the `fill_never` interval.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo/accept-a-payment, the 2026-11-07 base capture provides navigation to seven variants (new raw lines 9-21). React Native already had a May guide body (old raw lines 1793-1805 and old raw lines 1922-2004). source-stripe-oxxo-accept-payment.md should preserve the 2026-05-07 variants and date their claims. Checkout form completion creates a payable voucher, while later Checkout async success corresponds to the associated PaymentIntent succeeding (old raw lines 172-194). Mobile and Direct API client confirmation can issue or display the voucher before server-side confirmation of cash payment (old raw lines 1429-1487 and old raw lines 2294-2307). The May Legacy Direct API is described as supported and discouraged, with deprecation conditional, and needs both full name and email (old raw lines 2077-2083 and old raw lines 2195-2221). The voucher's `expires_after` cutoff ends the customer's ability to pay, with `processing` and eventual failure notification separate (old raw lines 2294-2307 and old raw lines 2396-2407). The May `fill_never` row gives 1 business day plus 2 calendar days for failure webhook arrival and explicitly says production and test mode match for that row. The interval describes that scenario's notification rather than the general voucher lifetime or production failure schedule (old raw lines 2345-2347). Reciprocal warnings belong on the acceptance and product overview routes and in `wiki/concepts/stripe-vouchers.md:97-107`. The May Checkout and Direct API variants document MX business scope and a 3-day default (old raw lines 20-37, old raw lines 105-107, old raw lines 2077-2083, and old raw lines 2191-2193). The separate November OXXO product overview lists accounts in Mexico, the United States, Canada and Singapore, with EEA and UK private preview, and a 5-day product default with a 1–7-day PaymentIntent override (`raw/stripe-payments-oxxo-2026-11-07.md:9-18`). The November accept index cannot resolve current per-variant defaults or eligibility or refresh SDK requirements. The May overview pairs next-business-day confirmation and settled funds (`raw/stripe-oxxo-2025.md:8-10`). The November overview distinguishes confirmation by next business day from settlement, with Tuesday–Thursday payments settling the following Monday and Friday–Monday payments the following Wednesday, listed as up to four business days (T+4) (`raw/stripe-payments-oxxo-2026-11-07.md:15-23`). The captures establish these dated documentation claims rather than actual account access, voucher payment or settlement.
